dialogue.Introduction: Well hello there, @! Welcome to the Oasis. I am the Dye Trader, the most fabulous dyer for a thousand miles of sand.$h#$b#Need a color? Everything in my tent is dyed to perfection, darling.$h
dialogue.Mon: Monday in the desert means fresh batches cooking in the dye vat. The whole Oasis smells of cinnamon and a little bit of regret.$h
dialogue.Tue: Tuesday I trade with the caravans. They always want cheaper dye, and I always say no. Color costs what color costs, darling.$a
dialogue.Wed: Hello, @. The Wizard came by and tried to buy my blue dye for his tower. I told him it is not magic, it is art, and he sulked for an hour.$u
dialogue.Thu: Thursday is for pattern testing. I dye a swatch, pin it to my turban, and stand very still so I can admire myself.$h
dialogue.Fri: The Merchant wandered out to see my wares yesterday and asked if the dyes were on sale. Darling, a dye trader never discounts. Not even for the Merchant.$s
dialogue.Sat: Saturday is market day. I am so busy I can barely keep up with my own orders. Oh well, that is the price of being fabulous.$h
dialogue.Sun: Sunday is quiet at the Oasis. I lounge on the cushions and let the vats cool. It is the only time I can hear the sand.$s
dialogue.Mon2: @, do you know why I wear a robe? Every dye I make stains my skin a little. I wear it so the stains look intentional.$u
dialogue.Wed2: I was thinking about your farm, @. A bolt of bright red for the barn roof would be fiery, bold and perfectly seasonal.$h
dialogue.Fri2: The mines bring me gems to dye with, and the goblins bring me trouble. I would rather have the gems, honestly.$h
dialogue.Tue6: Do you know, @, I trained in this desert for years before I learned to dye properly? My first batch turned my hands green and my cat purple.$h
dialogue.Thu6: Between us, the Tavernkeep has been asking me to dye the saloon curtains. I said I would think about it, which means yes.$h
dialogue.Sat6: The Steampunker keeps sending me gears to use as buttons. I like the idea, but my robe is busy enough as it is.$u
dialogue.Mon4: @, I have been wanting to say this for a while. You are one of the few who truly appreciate color. That makes you my favorite customer.$h
dialogue.Tue4: I hope you did not mind me wearing that bright orange last week. I wanted to see if anyone in town would notice. You did, and that is a compliment.$h
dialogue.Wed4: Some days the desert glare hurts my eyes. You are the only one who has ever asked why I wear so many shades of blue. I was honored.$l
dialogue.Thu4: Every time I finish a new dye I think of the Clothier and the Stylist, and whether they would be proud or horrified. Probably horrified, but in a good way.$h
dialogue.Fri4: I never told anyone this, but my first dye was a mess of mud and cactus juice. I still keep a jar of it on the shelf to remind me how far I have come.$s
dialogue.Sat4: I do miss the big desert cities sometimes. The bright markets and the noise. Out here it is quiet, and I am still learning to like the quiet.$s
dialogue.Sun4: Thank you for dropping by, @. The Oasis gets lonely when the caravans leave. Stay a while and we can pick out colors together.$h
dialogue.Mon8: @, I trust you more than I trust my own dye vat, and that is saying something. If you ever find a rare color, bring it to me first. I will pay you handsomely.$l
dialogue.Tue8: I used to think nobody would ever stop by the Oasis to see me. Then you came along, bumping into my vats and asking silly questions. I am glad you did.$l
dialogue.Wed8: I was afraid everyone in the valley thought I was a little too much. You are the first person who called my turban magnificent. I cried a little. Do not tell anyone.$s
dialogue.Thu8: When the Wall of Flesh fell I was scared. Those hardmode monsters came close to the desert. But I kept thinking of the colors we would see together, and it helped.$s
dialogue.Fri8: Some nights I wonder what I would be doing if I had never left the caravan. Probably dyeing tents for strangers and never meeting anyone as lovely as you, @.$l
dialogue.Sat8: @, you have a good eye for color. Never let anyone tell you a bright shade is wrong. Brightness is the whole point of living, my friend.$h
dialogue.Sun8: I keep thinking about the sunsets we watched from the dunes. My favorite dye is the one I have not made yet, and I think it is the color of that sky.$l
dialogue.Fri10: I have been dreaming of a dye so bright it makes the sun jealous. You are the only one I would show it to, @.$l
dialogue.Wed10: @, if you ever need a bright dye for a special day, I will make it myself. Nobody else in the valley would get the shade right.$h
dialogue.Sat10: I have decided, @, that you are the first person in this valley I will teach my secret blend. Do not repeat it. Ever.$l
dialogue.summer_Wed: Summer Wednesdays are hot enough to melt the dye right off the bolts. I have started dyeing in the shade, and it is terribly inconvenient.$a
dialogue.fall_Fri: The autumn leaves inspire my new colors. I dyed a cloth the exact shade of a pumpkin. I am thrilled, and my cat is mortified.$h
dialogue.winter_Sun: Winter in the Calico Desert is not really winter, but I still get cold at night. I bundle up in scarves dyed crimson for courage.$h
dialogue.spring_Sat: Spring brings flowers, and I cannot get enough of them. I dye petals for the flower sellers. They tell me it makes their roses look richer.$h
dialogue.summer_Tue: Summer Tuesday, and the Oasis is at its brightest. Every color looks twice as vivid under this sun, and I have never been happier.$h
dialogue.winter_Fri8: @, I dreamed last night that you and I painted the whole desert pink. Then the sand turned to snow and we painted that too. A strange dream, but a sweet one.$l
dialogue.spring_5: Early spring is perfect for pastel dyes. The desert is full of color at last, and so am I.$h
dialogue.summer_14: Midsummer, and the caravans are running late. Still, I have plenty of color to keep me busy while I wait for them.$h
dialogue.fall_15: Fall in the desert is short and beautiful. I dyed my cushions burnt orange to match the sunsets over the dunes.$h
dialogue.winter_20: Winter twentieth, and the Oasis is so quiet I can hear the vats bubbling. It is peaceful in a way I did not expect.$h
dialogue.winter_3: Winter third. I started a new batch of blue dye today. It is the color of the cold night sky, and I am quite proud of it.$h

rainy: Rain in the desert? Darling, this is a dye trader's nightmare. Every drop smears my fresh colors, so I am stuck indoors cursing the sky.$a

situations.eye: That giant eyeball is finally gone. I dyed a cloth in its honor. It is a rather murderous violet, and I am thrilled.$h
situations.evilBoss: The Eater of Worlds and the Brain of Cthulhu are both gone, or at least the brain is. Their ichor makes a dreadful dye, so I am scrubbing my vats twice.$a
situations.skeletron: The old skull has been put to rest and the dungeon is open. The Old Man came by my tent asking for a dye to match his beard. Hot pink, if you can believe it.$u
situations.queenBee: The Queen Bee is gone. Her honey shade is a gorgeous amber, and I have already bottled a batch of it for the caravans.$h
situations.hardmode: The Wall of Flesh has fallen and hardmode has begun. The Hallow glows with colors nobody has ever dyed before, so I must go hunting for them.$u
situations.mechs: A mechanical menace was smashed last night. I gathered the shiny bits and I am making the most dazzling silver dye in the valley.$h
situations.plantera: Plantera is defeated and the jungle temple is open. The jungle greens are glorious, and I need to get in there before my vine dye runs out.$h
situations.golem: The Golem has fallen apart. I collected a stone that gleams with sun-gold, and now I am dyeing a robe in its honor.$h
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist is defeated and the celestial pillars stand over the valley. Their glow is the most theatrical color I have ever seen.$u
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord is gone and the sky is clean again. I have dyed a hundred bolts of cloth in the deepest shade of night blue.$h
situations.goblins: The goblin army has been repelled. They left behind a stack of fabulous cloth and a lingering smell of smoke.$a
situations.pirates: The pirates were sent packing. They tried to buy dye for their sails and I refused, unless they paid in gold. They did not have any gold.$h
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion ran off. I dyed a whole row of scarves icy blue to keep my nerves steady.$s
situations.martians: The Martians are gone. Their saucer lamps were dazzling but dreadfully ugly, so I am making dyes that clash with everything they wore.$a
situations.bloodMoon: Last night the moon turned red. That is a color I could never match, so I stayed inside and dyed everything crimson just to be safe.$s
situations.eclipse: The sun went dark last night. I wore black for the whole eclipse, which was the perfect excuse for a new robe.$h
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party today. I am bringing rainbow dye for the streamers, and nobody can say no to that.$h

festivals.spring13: Egg dyeing is an art, @. Most people use boring onion skins. I bring the good stuff, and it makes the eggs shimmer like jewels.$h
festivals.spring24: A Flower Dance needs color. Let me dress you in something that will make the whole town turn and look.$h
festivals.summer11: I have added a bottle of my finest sunset red to the community soup. It is not for drinking, but nobody has complained yet.$h
festivals.summer28: Look at the jellies glowing blue and pink. I could never dye the sea that vivid, so I just admire it from the sand.$s
festivals.fall16: My display at the grange has a whole wall of dyed fabrics, and everyone is trying to guess my secret ingredient. It is dye, obviously.$h
festivals.fall27: Spirit's Eve is my favorite. Dye the sheets a ghostly grey, dye the candles green, and wander the maze like a proper specter.$h
festivals.winter8: The ice fishing is not my thing, but the snow sculptures take dye beautifully. Frosted turquoise, darling.$h
festivals.winter25: I received a secret gift this year, a vial of dye that changes color in the light. I have no idea who sent it, but I am thrilled.$u

loved.text: Oh my! That is the most gorgeous thing I have ever been handed. You have impeccable taste, and I will treasure this forever.$l

liked.text: Lovely, @. This would make a perfectly fabulous accent for my turban. Thank you.$h

neutral.text: Oh, thank you. It is not quite my shade, but a dye trader can always find a use for a little extra.$h

disliked.text: Oh. Well. This is not something a dye trader can work with, I am afraid. Think of me next time.$a

hated.text: Are you trying to insult me? This is the ugliest thing I have seen since the Martian lamps. Take it away this instant!$a

events.after: Careful with that violet on your sleeves, darling. It does not come out of anything.

steps.say: Oh! @, you came all the way across the sand. Welcome to my tent, such as it is.$h
Mind the floor. Cloth is drying everywhere, and it stains quite badly.$a
Look! I am testing a swatch of violet. It is the finest violet in the desert, and you are the first to see it.$h

steps.question: What do you think of the violet?

answers.reply: Right? I knew you had taste.$h
A bruise? Darling, it is a royal bruise.$a

steps.say: Here, take this. Every adventurer should own a proper dye vat. Just do not spill it on your shirt.$h

events.after: If the Merchant tries to sell you paint as dye, do not believe a word of it.

steps.say: @! The sun is out and I came for a walk. Fine colors deserve fine weather.$h
Oh, it is the Dye Trader again. Did you come to buy something, or to make me look bad in those robes?$a
A dye trader needs sunshine to judge a color properly. You would not understand.$h
Did you know the Merchant once tried to sell me a bucket of paint as premium dye? I may never forgive him.$a

steps.question: Do you think he cheated you?

answers.reply: Thank you, @. Somebody finally agrees with me.$h
Honest? Perhaps I am the only one who finds him hard to trust.$s

steps.say: Anyway, let us look at the sunset from the bridge. The colors are fabulous.$h

events.after: Ask the Tavernkeep for the pink mug, it is my idea and he hates it.

steps.say: Evening, @. The Stardrop Saloon is the only place in the valley where a dye trader can have a drink without anyone asking about his turban.$h
Another round for the desert fellow, and this time put some color in the glass, my friend.$h
I think color belongs in drinks too. A pink mug is just a glass with attitude.$h
I am a little homesick tonight, @. Back in the desert every night looked like this, all stars and sand.$s
Stop being so gloomy. You have a whole valley full of people who think you are magnificent, darling.$h

answers.reply: Then we will bring a little desert home to you. Next time I bring sand.$s

answers.text: Not at all, this place is great.
answers.reply: Good. You are making me braver about it, @.$h

steps.say: Let me buy you a drink, the saloon's finest. I insist. It is about time I spent some coin.$h

events.after: I still think about those dunes at sunset. Do not let me get sentimental in front of the Tavernkeep.

steps.say: @, sit down, please. You look like you walked the whole valley. I made you a cup of tea with a little blue dye in it. Perfectly safe, I promise.$h
I was not always a dye trader, you know. I started out selling robes in the Calico Desert. The rain never came and nobody bought a single one.$s
So I learned to make colors nobody else could. Sunset orange, midnight blue, and a green that looks like a wet cactus. It is my signature.$h
When I left the caravan, I thought I would be alone forever. Then you came to this Oasis, and I finally had someone to show my colors to.$l

steps.question: Will you come see the dunes with me at sunset?

answers.reply: Wonderful. Bring a blanket, the sand gets cold.$l
That is fine, my friend. I will wait a little longer.$s

steps.say: Thank you for listening to an old dyer, @. You are one of the good ones.$h

events.after: The sea is the best color in the world, and you are the best company for looking at it.

steps.say: @, the beach is such a bright place. Look at all the blues the water makes. I had to come see it with you.$h
Oi, dye man! You are blocking my fishing line. Move your fabulous robe, I need the light.$a
Dear child, your line is perfectly safe. You may have the light. I will admire the sea from here.$h
The sea gave me my most cherished color. A deep teal, like the water right before a storm. I wish I could bottle it for you, @.$h
Bottle the sea? That is the silliest thing I ever heard. Silly grown-ups.$h

steps.question: Would you like to watch the sea with me again?

answers.reply: Every day? Then you will have to dye your boots sea green too.$l
Once a season is plenty, I suppose. The sea waits for no one.$s

steps.say: Thank you, @. This was a perfect day, and I hope you know that.$l
